dedupe_keys.name: sicin synthetic interdependent critical infrastructure networks generator

description: SICIN generates synthetic systems of interdependent gas, power and water networks as test cases for vulnerability and restoration studies when real network data are confidential. It places facilities with a modified simulated annealing algorithm, links them with degree sequences learned from real networks, creates interdependent links, and initialises flows with a non-linear optimisation solved by IPOPT. Yu Wang, Jin-Zhu Yu and Hiba Baroud of Vanderbilt University developed it and published it in the IEEE Systems Journal in 2021, benchmarking against the real Shelby County, Tennessee networks and a system in Xiamen; SICIN's networks came closest to the real ones on most topology metrics over 300 realisations. Coverage is any area with tract population data. Format and access: Python scripts for topology and Julia for flow optimisation on a public code repository with the data used. Licence: no licence file found; free to read. Caveats: without a licence reuse terms are unclear, and the repository is not maintained as a package. It supports network flow, cascading failure and restoration testbeds. Related catalogue records are the I2Sim simulator and the IN-CORE interdependency functionality.
